- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 1–2% for the next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract sentiment-driven downward bias.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) when sentiment is volatile; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce lag.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5–7 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture the peak; cap forecast at +1.5% above recent high unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 5-day window as anchor for correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.7 → -0.3 → +0.6), model overreacts; apply dampening factor of 0.85 to forecast weights for such periods.
